facts.statement: Hamipterus was an extinct pterosaur living in the Early Cretaceous in northwestern China.
facts.quote: Hamipterus is an extinct genus of pteranodontoid pterosaurs from the Early Cretaceous Shengjinkou Formation of northwestern China.

facts.statement: Hamipterus is a monotypic genus containing only the single species Hamipterus tianshanensis.
facts.quote: It is a monotypic genus known from a single species, the type species, H. tianshanensis.

facts.statement: The species Hamipterus tianshanensis was formally named and described in 2014 by a team of researchers including Wang Xiaolin and Alexander Kellner.
facts.quote: In 2014, the type species Hamipterus tianshanensis was named and described by Wang Xiaolin, Alexander Kellner, Jiang Shunxing, Wang Qiang, Ma Yingxia, Yahefujiang Paidoula, Cheng Xin, Taissa Rodrigues, Meng Xi, Zhang Jialiang, Li Ning, and Zhou Zhonghe.

facts.statement: The species name tianshanensis refers to the Tian Shan mountain range where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: The specific name refers to the provenance from the Tian Shan, a mountain range.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is a skull from the Lower Cretaceous Tugulu Group, likely belonging to a female.
facts.quote: The holotype, IVPP V18931.1, has been found in a layer of the Tugulu Group dating from the Lower Cretaceous. It consists of a skull, probably of a female.

facts.statement: Excavations secured eleven blocks of fossils containing at least 40 individuals, including soft tissue remnants like horn sheaths.
facts.quote: Eleven such blocks had in 2014 been secured, numbered IVPP V18931 to V18941. Together, they comprise the remains of at least 40 animals, both bones and soft tissue remnants such as the horn sheaths of skull crests.

facts.statement: Five uncrushed eggs were found at the site alongside the adult fossils.
facts.quote: Five uncrushed eggs were also found.

facts.statement: Individuals of Hamipterus had a wingspan ranging from 1.5 to 3.5 meters.
facts.quote: The wingspan of the individuals described in 2014 ranged from 1.5 - 3.5 m.

facts.statement: The dentary bone of the lower jaw features a distinctive hook-shaped process.
facts.quote: The dentary, the front bone of the lower jaw, has a hook-shaped process.

facts.statement: The rear top of the skull bears a well-developed crest on the central supraoccipital bone.
facts.quote: The central supraoccipital of the top rear skull bears a well-developed crest.

facts.statement: Hamipterus possessed very thin tooth enamel that covered only about half of the tooth crown.
facts.quote: The tooth enamel of Hamipterus was very thin. It only covered about half of the tooth crown.

facts.statement: Researchers assumed sexual dimorphism existed, with larger males sporting larger crests than smaller females.
facts.quote: It was assumed that a clear sexual dimorphism was discovered, with the largest specimens sporting the largest crests being the males, while smaller individuals were females with smaller crests.

facts.statement: A 2021 study disputes earlier claims of parental care, showing that young Hamipterus did not differ significantly from other flight-capable hatchlings.
facts.quote: However, this study has since been criticized by some paleontologists. A 2021 study further disagrees by demonstrating that the young of Hamipterus don't differ significantly from the other flight capable flaplings.

facts.statement: Hamipterus is classified within the suborder Pterodactyloidea and the group Pteranodontoidea.
facts.quote: Hamipterus was within the Pterodactyloidea, placed into the group Pteranodontoidea.

facts.statement: Cladistic analyses have recovered Hamipterus within the family Hamipteridae.
facts.quote: In the analyses, they recovered this genus within the family Hamipteridae.

facts.statement: The large number of fossils allowed scientists to establish a growth series showing how the animals developed through their life stages.
facts.quote: The large number of individuals found allowed the establishment of a growth series, showing how individuals developed through their ontogeny.

facts.statement: The wingspan of described individuals ranges from 1.5 to 3.5 meters.
facts.quote: La envergadura alar de los individuos descritos varía de 1.5 a 3.5 metros.

facts.statement: The dentary bone of the jaw possesses a hook-shaped process.
facts.quote: El dentario, el hueso frontal de la mandíbula, tiene un proceso en forma de gancho.

facts.statement: The central supraoccipital at the top-rear of the skull features a well-developed crest.
facts.quote: El supraoccipital central en la parte superior-posterior del cráneo posee una cresta bien desarrollada.

facts.statement: The humerus is perforated by a pneumatic foramen near the base of the deltopectoral crest.
facts.quote: El húmero está perforado por un foramen neumático cerca de la base de la cresta deltopectoral.

facts.statement: The lower external carpal bone of the wrist has a spine-shaped process pointing downward.
facts.quote: El hueso carpiano externo inferior de la muñeca tiene un proceso en forma de espina que apunta hacia abajo.

facts.statement: Both the tip of the snout and the jaw are slightly expanded.
facts.quote: Tanto la punta del hocico como de la mandíbula están levemente expandidas.

facts.statement: Hamipterus is classified within Pterodactyloidea and placed in the clade Pteranodontoidea.
facts.quote: Hamipterus está clasificado dentro de Pterodactyloidea, situado en el clado Pteranodontoidea.

facts.statement: A cladistic analysis could not precisely resolve its relationships with Istiodactylus, Ludodactylus, and the family Anhangueridae.
facts.quote: Un análisis cladístico sin embargo no pudo resolver de manera precisa sus relaciones con respecto a Istiodactylus, Ludodactylus y la familia Anhangueridae.

facts.statement: The species lived during the Valanginian stage, between 137.05 and 132.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Valanginian to Valanginian (137.05 to 132.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Four fossil occurrences of this genus have been recorded.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 4

facts.statement: Wang et al. (2026) described an articulated forelimb from Lower Cretaceous strata in Xinjiang, China, providing new anatomical information.
facts.quote: Wang et al. (2026) describe an articulated forelimb of Hamipterus tianshanensis from the Lower Cretaceous strata in Xinjiang (China), providing new information on the anatomy of members of this species.

facts.statement: The large number of individuals found allowed the establishment of an ontogenetic series showing how the animals developed as they matured.
facts.quote: El enorme número de individuos hallados permitió el establecimiento de una serie ontogénica, mostrando cómo los individuos se desarrollaban a medida que iban madurando.

facts.statement: It is presumed there was clear sexual dimorphism where larger specimens with large crests were males and smaller individuals with smaller crests were females.
facts.quote: Se presume que había un claro dimorfismo sexual en esta especie, en el que los mayores especímenes con grandes crestas eran los machos y los individuos pequeños con crestas menores serían las hembras.

facts.statement: If this presumption is correct, it would refute the hypothesis that only males possessed crests in pterosaurs.
facts.quote: De ser así, sería una refutación a la hipótesis de que en los pterosaurios, solo los machos poseían crestas.
